clue.text: Many a special feature of the garden is brought to the table

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many

parts.words: a special feature of the garden
parts.note: a garden bed of stones and alpine plants

explanation.surface: Some striking ornament from the garden is carried indoors and set on the dining table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many a' reads as one phrase meaning 'many'; the setter splits it so Many supplies a numeral and 'a special feature' starts the garden part.
explanation.definitionFit: Plates, cups and dishes are what get carried out and laid for a meal, so earthenware tableware fits.

clue.text: The court's opening lines

parts.note: an opening is an opportunity or chance
railway lines, abbreviated RY

explanation.surface: It reads like a question about how a trial begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening lines' looks like the first words of a speech, but the two words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Chancery was a division of the English High Court, presided over by the Lord Chancellor.

clue.text: A clothier striking a craftsman

parts.note: workers out are on strike
a skilled worker who assembles machine parts

explanation.surface: A tailor or a skilled tradesman has walked off the job.
explanation.walkthrough: Striking seems to mean impressive, but it means on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfitter sells clothes and equipment, a shop or dealer in garments like a clothier.

clue.text: Bends are OK in the country

indicators.note: bent things are twisted out of shape, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: all five letters

explanation.surface: Curves in the road are fine out in rural areas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The country' suggests the countryside, but it means a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Korea is an East Asian nation, now divided into North and South, so it fits a definition naming a state.

clue.text: When about 50 relax — let go
A dog set onto scholars

parts.note: BAs, holders of a Bachelor of Arts degree
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sets a dog on a group of academics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set onto' sounds like urging a dog to attack, but it means the word set is placed after the scholars.
explanation.definitionFit: A basset is a short-legged hound breed with long ears, an example of the general class dog.

clue.text: The supporters present accommodated in new stand

indicators.note: accommodated in means given room inside, so one piece sits within the other
a new form is a changed one, so these letters are put in a fresh order

parts.note: here means present, in attendance
the letters of stand rearranged

explanation.surface: Fans in attendance are housed in a newly built grandstand.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sets up a football ground, with supporters and a stand; both words are doing other jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Adherents are followers who stick to a cause or leader, people who back it like supporters.

clue.text: Deposed head of state, very weary
The people close at hand second the propositions

parts.note: these, the ones nearby rather than those over there
S, the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: The people nearby back the motions being proposed.
explanation.walkthrough: Second sounds like the verb to support a motion, but it gives a single abbreviated letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesis is a statement put forward to be argued and defended, a proposition for debate.

clue.text: Getting explosive about drink as a gift

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the explosive goes round the drink

parts.note: TNT, trinitrotoluene
ale is beer

explanation.surface: Someone receives explosives wrapped round a bottle as a present.
explanation.walkthrough: The drink goes in after the first letter of the explosive.
explanation.definitionFit: A talent is a natural aptitude or flair, which we also call a gift.

clue.text: Player in a satisfactory position

indicators.note: in says the wanted letters sit inside the following word, waiting to be lifted out

parts.note: the run of letters after satisf- in this word

explanation.surface: A sportsman is well placed on the field.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'in a satisfactory position' as the hiding place: the five letters sit inside satisfactory.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is someone who performs a part on stage, the sense shared with a performer in drama.

clue.text: This is disgusting — home's a lot different

indicators.note: something made different is changed, so these letters are rearranged into another order

parts.note: all nine letters, the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone recoils at a house that has changed beyond recognition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something loathsome provokes revulsion and hatred, exactly the reaction a repellent thing causes.

clue.text: Chapter well-informed about popular I ac

definitions.note: OCR-garbled: the printed definition is lost in the scan; the answer is fixed by the wordplay and every crossing

indicators.note: about means going round, so the well-informed word wraps itself round the popular word

parts.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for chapter
someone aware knows what is going on
in, fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A book chapter shows knowledge of what is fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan garbles the last word of this clue, so the definition is lost. Chapter and well-informed together surround popular, giving CH-IN-AWARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinaware means porcelain cups, plates and dishes, so the lost definition was some term for crockery or pottery.

clue.text: Limits the area for stock

definitions.note: plural noun; the answer is singular, as in 'the range of a gun'
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the extent or scope between bounds
second meaning: open grazing land for cattle

explanation.surface: Fences mark out where the farm animals may roam.
explanation.walkthrough: Stock here is livestock, not shares or goods in a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the span between outer limits and, in North America especially, open land where cattle graze.

clue.text: Desert people's competitive activity

parts.note: to rat is to desert or betray one's side
a people or nation

explanation.surface: Tribes who live in the desert have their own contests.
explanation.walkthrough: Desert looks like a noun, sandy wasteland, but it is the verb to abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the fierce, endless struggle for success in modern working life, a competitive scramble.

clue.text: Fear not — no changes to make this time

indicators.note: changes here means altered forms, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: all nine letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A reassurance that nothing will be altered on this occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This time' reads as 'on this occasion'; it is the definition, a time of day.
explanation.definitionFit: The afternoon is a particular part of the day, between noon and evening, so it is one stretch of the clock.

clue.text: Holding catch for return to the river

indicators.note: something returned comes back the way it went, so this word is read from its end

parts.note: to net is to catch
the Ure, a Yorkshire river and a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: An angler keeps a fish to put it back in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: Catch and return sound like fishing; return is the signal to turn the net round.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenure is the holding of an office or property, so a noun for possession over a period fits.

clue.text: Soldiers charge in a lull

parts.note: the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
a charge is a duty or task entrusted, a mission

explanation.surface: Troops attack during a quiet spell in the fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: Charge looks like an attack, which suits soldiers, but means an assigned task.
explanation.definitionFit: Remission is a temporary easing, as of a disease's symptoms, which is a lull or abatement.

clue.text: Its purpose is to contain a fire

definitions.text: Its purpose is to contain a fire

parts.words: Its purpose is to contain a fire
parts.note: surface reading: something whose job is to hold a fire, like a grate
setter's reading: to keep a fire in check, as a fireproof mineral lining does

explanation.walkthrough: Contain reads as hold inside, like a hearth; it also means restrain, which fireproofing does.
explanation.definitionFit: This fibrous mineral was long used for fire-resistant insulation and safety curtains because it does not burn.

clue.text: Wriggle out of summons to the Governor

parts.note: a writ is a legal summons
His Excellency, the title of a colonial governor

explanation.surface: Someone tries to evade being called before the Governor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wriggle out of' looks like one phrase meaning evade, but the definition is Wriggle alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To writhe is to twist the body about, as in pain, which is what wriggling describes.

clue.text: Specialist who's no longer bold

parts.note: ex, former
pert, cheeky or forward

explanation.surface: An authority figure who has lost their nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert is a person with deep knowledge of a field, a specialist in it.

clue.text: Imagines a fool will accept total direction

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an ass is a fool
a sum is a total
east, one of the compass points

explanation.surface: Someone foolish thinks they will be handed complete control.
explanation.walkthrough: The total and the direction go in together between the second and third letters of the fool.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume is to suppose or take for granted, the same as imagining something is so.

clue.text: Cold wind — Easterly
Wicked illumination!

parts.note: surface reading: evil, or slang for brilliant
setter's reading: having a wick, a light source that burns one

explanation.walkthrough: Wicked is read literally as 'fitted with a wick'.
explanation.definitionFit: A wax stick with a wick through its centre gives light when lit, an old form of illumination.

clue.text: Moving song about a high-minded individual

indicators.note: about means around, so the song wraps itself round the person

parts.note: an air is a tune or song
a saint, abbreviated ST

explanation.surface: A stirring song tells of a person of lofty principles.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving reads as emotionally touching, but it means up and about.
explanation.definitionFit: Astir means up and in motion, out of bed and active, so it describes something that is moving.

clue.text: A liking for sensation

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the flavour perceived by the tongue

explanation.surface: Someone loves a thrill.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a fondness or preference and the sense by which flavour is perceived on the tongue.

clue.text: Getting a job as the alternative — and quickly!

indicators.note: an alternative version is a different arrangement, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: a post is a job
the five letters of these two words rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone urges taking a job instead, and fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As the alternative' reads as 'instead'; in fact 'as the' supplies the letters and alternative tells you to rearrange them.
explanation.definitionFit: Posthaste is an old adverb meaning with all speed, from the urgent pace of riders carrying the mail.

clue.text: A flighty poet?

parts.note: surface reading: a fickle, scatterbrained versifier
setter's reading: one that flies home, a racing pigeon, sharing its name with the Greek epic poet

explanation.walkthrough: Flighty usually means fickle; here it means given to flight, as a racing pigeon is.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek epic poet of the Iliad shares his name with a homing pigeon, a bird bred to fly back.

clue.text: Underworld procedure, so to speak

parts.note: Dis, the Roman god of the underworld and his realm
a course of action is a procedure

explanation.surface: It sounds like a remark about how gangsters operate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So to speak' is a stock phrase; here speak alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To discourse is to talk at length on a subject, a formal verb for speaking.

clue.text: Damp is needed for raising Nigella

parts.note: the mist in which that love sits
the plant's common name is love-in-a-mist; love is O, nil in tennis

explanation.surface: A gardener notes that damp conditions are needed to grow nigella.
explanation.walkthrough: Nigella is the flower known as love-in-a-mist; taking that name literally puts O inside MIST. Raising is growing a plant, not lifting.
explanation.definitionFit: Moist means slightly wet, the same as damp.

clue.text: Cast off

parts.note: surface reading: discarded, or freeing a boat from its moorings
setter's reading: the actors leave the stage, the stage direction in Latin

explanation.walkthrough: Cast looks like a verb but is the company of actors; off is where they go.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin stage direction meaning 'they go out' tells several players to leave the stage together.

clue.text: Barges in, maybe charges

indicators.note: maybe hints the words could be otherwise, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: all eight letters of both words

explanation.surface: Someone who barges in might be launching an attack.
explanation.walkthrough: Charges here are heraldic: the devices displayed on a coat of arms.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry, the emblems on a shield are called both charges and bearings, synonyms in that specialist vocabulary.
